claim:sbml-in-tellurium.proposition: Monolithic Tellurium reproduces the reference to ~1e-6 and is the fastest approach — the speed + accuracy reference.
claim:sbml-in-tellurium.hypothesis: A single TelluriumProcess matches direct libroadrunner to near machine tolerance and is the fastest approach; it defines the accuracy and speed reference for every other study.

claim:mechanical-split-cost.proposition: Mechanical-split (additive-coupling) error is real and shrinks monotonically with the coupling interval (max relative error 0.857 at 0.1 → 0.112 at 0.0125 → 0.0066 at 0.001, measured against the monolithic reference); a clean split was only possible across the weakly-coupled glycogen/trehalose sinks — splitting across the strong P/ATP/ADP energy coupling diverges.
claim:mechanical-split-cost.hypothesis: Additive (Jacobi) coupling introduces a real splitting error that decreases monotonically as the coupling interval shrinks, at the cost of extra orchestration - isolating vivarium's overhead with no change to the biology.

claim:biological-modular-seam.proposition: A biological-seam decomposition reproduces the reference (0.468 → 0.100 as the coupling step shrinks, T=0.15) as a GENUINE multi-process composition — the first point on the spectrum where the model is composable.
claim:biological-modular-seam.hypothesis: A biological upper/lower partition, reconciled additively through the real process-bigraph apply path, reproduces the reference within tolerance and is genuinely composable (two independent process nodes, not one process with an internal loop).

claim:fully-native-pbg.proposition: A fully native process-bigraph implementation reaches reference fidelity (~1e-7); at 17 species the scalar-dict-vs-array leaf choice is perf-irrelevant (only bites at 100s-1000s of species).
claim:fully-native-pbg.hypothesis: A hand-ported native RHS integrated by scipy matches the reference to high fidelity; at 17 species the scalar-dict vs numpy-array leaf choice is perf-irrelevant.

claim:cross-engine-coupling.proposition: A single composite runs HALF in one engine and HALF in another, sharing one store - structurally impossible for a monolith. Swapping the lower half of the seam=aldolase composite from Tellurium to COPASI or to the native process reproduces the Tellurium+Tellurium trajectory at the same coupling interval (0.005) to max relative error 3.2e-7 (COPASI 3.19e-7, native 3.20e-7, measured); the engines are interchangeable at a seam as a ~1e-7 drop-in (COPASI is not bit-reproducible run to run). This is the composability payoff, not a numeric result.
claim:cross-engine-coupling.hypothesis: A hybrid composite (upper glycolysis in Tellurium, lower glycolysis in COPASI or the native process) sharing one species store runs through process-bigraph and reproduces the biological-seam result - the engine at either side of the seam is a drop-in, the composability payoff a monolith can never match.

claim:ensemble-and-multirate.proposition: A Ray ensemble of monoliths gives a real 7.5x wall-clock speedup on 16 cores — the one study where vivarium wins on speed; libroadrunner does NOT release the GIL, so in-process threads cannot (they backfire). Separately, process-bigraph #270's event-heap scheduler is bit-identical to the stock scan loop (same math, different tick order) and its wall-clock advantage grows monotonically with P on a genuinely multi-rate composite — measured 0.98x at P=4 (heap bookkeeping with nothing to gain), crossing over near P~50-64, to 1.64x at P=256 on real libroadrunner/CVODE instances. The per-process CVODE integration dominates the per-tick scan until P reaches the low hundreds, so the multiplier is modest at the P a unit test can afford; it is reported as measured, and the regime where it grows large (hundreds-to-thousands of cheap processes) is #270's own 4.8x@P=100 -> 46x@P=1000 micro-benchmark, cited not reproduced.
claim:ensemble-and-multirate.hypothesis: A Ray-backed same-rate ensemble of monoliths delivers a real wall-clock speedup (libroadrunner does not release the GIL, so only OS-process parallelism helps); and the #270 heap scheduler runs the SAME math as the scan loop (bit-identical) with a wall-clock advantage that grows with the instance count P on a multi-rate ensemble.

claim:bigger-models-and-abm-limit.proposition: The one strong, well-measured result is that the MONOLITHIC libroadrunner BUILD strains superlinearly in the reaction count: 0.20 s at 97 species -> 1.76 s at 385 -> 5.54 s at 769 -> 18.5 s at 1537 species (~94x for ~16x the reactions, ~O(N^1.64)), with the dense-CVODE run blowing up alongside it (0.0023 s -> 2.56 s). That is the real strain point and the reason a very large SBML model is painful to run monolithically. Decomposition is NOT a free win: building N small models is SLOWER than the single compile up to ~100 species (1.7x slower at 97 species), reaches only rough parity at 385 species (1.40 vs 1.76 s) and becomes a clear build win only at ~1500 species (2.4x); and the decomposed per-tick RUN overhead is ~16x the monolith's CVODE run, so the decomposed body is SLOWER END-TO-END at every N measured (decomp_total 2.35 s vs mono_total 1.81 s at 385 species). The end-to-end gap narrows with N but the decomposed run is unmeasured past N=128, so no end-to-end crossover is claimed. Decomposition is a structural trade — it swaps the monolith's superlinear build for much higher run overhead — that would only pay off end-to-end on models larger than measured. CRUCIAL caveat: the additive-split accuracy is good only at small N / fine interval (max_rel_err 2e-3 at N=2, 1.2e-2 at N=8, 5.2e-2 at N=32) and is 0.31 (31%) at N=128 — so the regime where the speed gap narrows and the regime of acceptable accuracy do NOT co-occur at a fixed coupling interval. All numbers measured, not fabricated. ALSO: An agent-based model reduces to an SBML/Tellurium mean-field ODE ONLY in the large-population, well-mixed, deterministic limit; it structurally cannot capture stochasticity, discreteness, extinction, or individual heterogeneity. MEASURED (Lotka-Volterra, base rates r=a=b=m=1, start density (1.8, 1.0), horizon ~2 periods, seed 0): at a LARGE population scale K=400 (80 SSA runs) the mean-field ODE reproduces the SSA ensemble mean to a max relative error of 4.9% with 0% of runs seeing predator or total extinction — the reduction is VALID. At a SMALL scale K=8 (200 SSA runs) the stochastic system collapses: the PREDATORS go extinct in 86.5% of runs and BOTH species in 51.0%, hitting absorbing states that the neutrally-stable ODE — which simply orbits forever, 0% extinction of either species at any K — can never reach, and the ensemble mean diverges several-fold from the ODE (predator-extinct runs let the prey escape, so the mean no longer resembles the bounded ODE cycle). The ODE additionally cannot represent the ensemble variance at ANY K. So "can an ABM be an SBML model?" has an honest, quantified answer: yes, but only as its large-population mean-field limit, and that reduction silently discards exactly the stochastic/discrete phenomena (extinction, demographic noise) that are often the biological point. This breaks the naive "just write it as SBML" claim.
claim:bigger-models-and-abm-limit.hypothesis: The monolithic libroadrunner build strains superlinearly (~O(N^1.6)) as the model scales, but decomposition is not a free win end-to-end; and a stochastic ABM reduces to an SBML/ODE only in the large-population, well-mixed, deterministic limit - at small population extinction and discreteness dominate and the ODE misses them entirely.

claim:decomposition-synthesis.proposition: The seven arms span a speed-accuracy-composability frontier with no dominant point; the tradeoff map + decision table turn that frontier into a regime-specific recommendation.
claim:decomposition-synthesis.hypothesis: No single arm dominates: the monolith is fastest+most accurate but least composable; native/biological seams trade speed for composability; the choice is regime-dependent and the tradeoff map makes the frontier explicit.

narrative.question: When you have a biochemical model, when should you run it monolithically in Tellurium (libroadrunner/CVODE) and when is it worth decomposing it into vivarium / process-bigraph sub-processes — and what does each point on that spectrum cost in performance and accuracy, buy in composability, and where does Tellurium (and SBML itself) stop being the right tool as models get larger or stop being reaction networks at all?
